correctness.rationale: Complete-multipartite spectral projector formula gives diagonal d=1/N+(1/p−1/N)F(Nh)+(1−1/p)F((N−p)h), distinct-vertex offdiagonal from strict chord-slope inequality. F has exact minimum (1−sqrt2)/2 at 4+3sqrt2, which bounds every N<=5 diagonal positive. For N>=7 the H(p,N−p) inequality yields a negative witness, N=6 p=3,4 have zero at witness with positive derivative and hence nearby negative. Quartic positive constant/linear/leading, negative cubic gives at most two positive roots by Descartes; positive endpoints plus negative witness force exactly two simple roots. Independently checked algebra/numeric sample boundary cases; not extrapolating experiments.

evidence: Bonaventura–Della Rocca derive finite radius of absolute monotonicity and hybrid positivity-preserving modifications for general systems. The Radau IIA complete-multipartite threshold is twelve vertices for a distinct method.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General SSP radius establishes sufficient small steps and possible global failures but not the profile-independent sharp N=5 threshold or every part’s exactly two positive roots.

originality.rationale: Standard SSP and absolute-monotonicity results concern arbitrary positive systems, while adjacent graph positivity classifications concern Radau IIA or Padé/RK4 stability functions. The exact unmodified TR-BDF2 threshold N=5 and single negative self-transition interval for each part are not implied by these sources.
